canonical_representation: Perseus item: markdown-like content plus typed widgets and widget options
learner_action_or_response: radio; numeric input; expression; categorizer; matcher; orderer; sorter; matrix; number line; interactive graph; code/program widgets; free response; other widgets
validation_and_assessment: widget-specific validators and scorers in a separate score registry
feedback_model: widget-specific correctness plus hints and item-level behavior
authoring_and_extension: new widget requires data-schema type, renderer, editor, optional validator/scorer, tests, accessibility docs and registration
renderer_runtime_boundary: content schema, renderer/editor and scoring packages are separated
mobile_offline_accessibility: explicit mobile and accessibility requirements; widget quality varies; some widgets include media and iframe capabilities
ARA_usefulness: Strong conceptual precedent for typed widgets, explicit user-input state and independent scoring; selected package reuse requires dependency and governance review
main_risks_or_limits: Large Khan-specific monorepo; heterogeneous legacy widgets; not accepting external contributions; some widgets violate ARA baseline media/security assumptions

canonical_representation: Versioned H5P libraries with machine names, dependencies and per-content-type semantics schemas
learner_action_or_response: content-type-specific actions such as drag/drop, selection and placement
validation_and_assessment: content-type code controls correctness, penalties, whole-task or per-element scoring
feedback_model: local feedback by drop zone, score-range feedback, retry/check behavior
authoring_and_extension: libraries are installed and versioned; semantics.json drives authoring forms and nested library fields
renderer_runtime_boundary: platform core loads content libraries and assets; each content type owns its runtime
mobile_offline_accessibility: localization fields and assistive labels exist; coordinate-heavy tasks and drag interactions require careful accessibility review
ARA_usefulness: Useful precedent for typed extension packages, authoring schemas and behavior settings
main_risks_or_limits: GPL core; per-library licensing; arbitrary library ecosystem expands attack and maintenance surface; some content models persist pixels and media

canonical_representation: JSON exam/question/part model with built-in and custom part types, extensions and diagnostic knowledge graph
learner_action_or_response: student-provided answers across part-specific input widgets; multipart and gap/step composition
validation_and_assessment: JME marking scripts, custom part marking, diagnostic algorithms and configurable feedback/reveal policies
feedback_model: part and exam feedback, advice, expected-answer and score visibility controls
authoring_and_extension: custom part types declare input widget, settings, marking script, extensions and whether usable as gap/step
renderer_runtime_boundary: browser runtime executes compiled assessment independently of editor
mobile_offline_accessibility: designed to run in browser; localization and accessibility need feature-level verification
ARA_usefulness: Strong precedent for custom response parts, diagnostics, explicit feedback policies and portable browser assessment
main_risks_or_limits: Maths-centred language and assessment architecture; custom scripts increase complexity and security review

canonical_representation: Question text plus student inputs, computer-algebra expressions and potential response trees
learner_action_or_response: student enters mathematical expressions, numbers, units, equivalence steps or free text
validation_and_assessment: separates input validity from mathematical correctness; deterministic CAS answer tests; multipart response trees and follow-through marking
feedback_model: feedback branches based on mathematical properties and common errors; partial credit possible
authoring_and_extension: teacher authors inputs, answer tests and potential response trees through Moodle/STACK tooling
renderer_runtime_boundary: Moodle question type and Maxima service are tightly coupled but conceptually separate input from assessment
mobile_offline_accessibility: web-based; accessibility and mobile depend on Moodle/input tools; server/CAS dependency limits offline use
ARA_usefulness: Essential conceptual precedent for validity-before-correctness, semantic answers, partial credit and property-based feedback
main_risks_or_limits: GPL/Moodle/Maxima coupling; domain-specific complexity; direct reuse would constrain architecture and offline profile

canonical_representation: Hierarchical courseware components with fields, children and runtime-provided services
learner_action_or_response: component-defined interaction; may embed problems, media or compound sequences
validation_and_assessment: component defines handlers and state; platform supplies runtime and storage conventions
feedback_model: component-specific
authoring_and_extension: Python class plugin API; deployable components can be nested and composed
renderer_runtime_boundary: explicit component/runtime layering
mobile_offline_accessibility: server-deployed architecture; offline/mobile/accessibility are component responsibilities
ARA_usefulness: Useful precedent for capability contracts, hierarchical composition and deployment governance
main_risks_or_limits: Arbitrary deployable code is incompatible with untrusted course JSON; server-heavy plugin model has substantial security and operations cost

canonical_representation: Editable semantic math field with export/import as LaTeX, MathML, ASCIIMath, Typst or MathJSON
learner_action_or_response: direct mathematical construction with keyboard, virtual keypad, selection and editing
validation_and_assessment: input component does not itself grade; MathJSON/compute-engine can support downstream semantic validation
feedback_model: speech-friendly rendering and interpretation preview can support validation feedback
authoring_and_extension: web components with events and customizable keyboard/macros
renderer_runtime_boundary: input/display component is separable from validator and course model
mobile_offline_accessibility: mobile-ready virtual keyboard; screen-reader support, ARIA and math-to-speech
ARA_usefulness: High-priority reusable candidate for mathematical input and accessible display
main_risks_or_limits: LaTeX permissiveness and multiple interchange formats require a canonical ARA representation and sanitization policy

canonical_representation: Interactive board of typed geometric, plotting and data-visualisation objects
learner_action_or_response: construct, drag and manipulate points, lines, functions and other objects
validation_and_assessment: library exposes object state and constraints but educational correctness must be supplied by ARA validators
feedback_model: visual state changes; educational feedback must be layered separately
authoring_and_extension: programmatic object creation; examples and Moodle/STACK integrations
renderer_runtime_boundary: geometry engine and renderer are reusable independently of an assessment model
mobile_offline_accessibility: multi-touch and browser support; accessibility of complex constructions requires dedicated design
ARA_usefulness: Strong reusable candidate for geometry/construction representations and manipulable responses
main_risks_or_limits: General-purpose imperative API can leak renderer details into content; no built-in pedagogical semantics or scoring

canonical_representation: Graph-theory data model with nodes, edges, collections, algorithms and optional renderer
learner_action_or_response: select, move, edit and analyse graph elements through application-defined interactions
validation_and_assessment: graph predicates and algorithms can support deterministic validators; library does not define educational scoring
feedback_model: application-defined
authoring_and_extension: extensions and layouts around a stable graph API
renderer_runtime_boundary: model can run headlessly while renderer is optional
mobile_offline_accessibility: interactive UI and extensions; accessibility must be designed by consuming application
ARA_usefulness: Strong reusable candidate for graph, network, automaton and causal-structure engines
main_risks_or_limits: Styling/layout APIs are broad; graph-theory model alone does not define domain grammar, learner task or accessible interaction

canonical_representation: CPython and package environment compiled to WebAssembly with JS-Python bridge
learner_action_or_response: execute Python and scientific packages inside browser
validation_and_assessment: runtime returns results/errors; tests and pedagogical assessment must be supplied separately
feedback_model: raw exceptions/output unless wrapped by educational layer
authoring_and_extension: package/runtime integration rather than course authoring
renderer_runtime_boundary: runtime can be isolated in workers and embedded under an ARA capability adapter
mobile_offline_accessibility: browser execution supports local operation after assets load; large payload and memory use; sandbox and network boundaries are critical
ARA_usefulness: Strong optional runtime candidate for executable Python and scientific tasks
main_risks_or_limits: Not an assessment system; supply-chain, resource limits, browser isolation and reproducible package versions require governance

canonical_representation: Code document plus runner, IO, debugger traces and optional test code
learner_action_or_response: edit, run, provide input, inspect output and debug Python/JavaScript
validation_and_assessment: test code can be appended; complete grading policy is outside the core runner
feedback_model: stdout, stderr, images and debugger trace; educational diagnostics require adapter
authoring_and_extension: web components and state API; slots allow surrounding controls
renderer_runtime_boundary: backend workers, communication, state and UI components are separated
mobile_offline_accessibility: browser-first; translations supported; COOP/COEP or service worker affects integration
ARA_usefulness: Strong reference and possible reusable component for code execution, trace and testing UX
main_risks_or_limits: Execution headers/service-worker requirements, package size, malicious code limits and test secrecy need explicit contracts

canonical_representation: Serialized workspace of typed interlocking blocks representing program structures
learner_action_or_response: construct, connect, reorder and edit blocks with drag, keyboard and screen reader interaction
validation_and_assessment: application can inspect generated code or workspace structure; educational validation is external
feedback_model: structural constraints and application-defined messages
authoring_and_extension: plugin ecosystem can add fields, renderers, themes and behaviors
renderer_runtime_boundary: workspace model, generator and renderer/plugin layers are separable
mobile_offline_accessibility: keyboard and screen-reader support with WCAG 2.2 conformance documentation
ARA_usefulness: Strong candidate for structured construction responses beyond programming, if domain block grammars are explicit
main_risks_or_limits: Block metaphors can oversimplify expert notations; large general API; serialization and plugin security require narrowing

canonical_representation: Markdown-inspired textual grammars compiled into more than twenty diagram types
learner_action_or_response: author or edit declarative diagram source; primarily representation rather than assessed manipulation
validation_and_assessment: parser and renderer validate syntax, not educational correctness
feedback_model: parse errors and rendered diagram; educational feedback external
authoring_and_extension: new diagram grammars and integrations are code-level extensions
renderer_runtime_boundary: text definition and renderer are separated; sandboxed rendering option exists
mobile_offline_accessibility: version-control friendly; accessibility varies by diagram type and generated output
ARA_usefulness: Useful conceptual precedent for declarative semantic grammars and reproducible diagrams
main_risks_or_limits: Not an educational model; grammars are heterogeneous; free-form syntax may be harder for learners and can expose unsupported styling/configuration

canonical_representation: Synchronized widget models and views connecting kernel state to browser components
learner_action_or_response: manipulate sliders, text boxes, toggles, plots, maps and custom widgets; explore parameter effects
validation_and_assessment: not an assessment system; validators can observe model state externally
feedback_model: continuous state feedback and domain visualization
authoring_and_extension: custom widget libraries share packaging and communication conventions
renderer_runtime_boundary: kernel model and browser view communicate through a protocol
mobile_offline_accessibility: browser notebook environment; custom widget accessibility/offline quality varies
ARA_usefulness: Strong precedent for capability manifests, synchronized state and simulation/control components
main_risks_or_limits: Kernel/server assumptions, arbitrary code and third-party widget variance conflict with a small secure offline core

canonical_representation: Courseware combining textbook text, algorithm visualisations and interactive automatically assessed exercises
learner_action_or_response: observe, manipulate and answer algorithm/data-structure tasks
validation_and_assessment: exercise-specific automatic assessment integrated with visualisations
feedback_model: immediate exercise feedback and progress integration
authoring_and_extension: Sphinx/RST courseware, JSAV visualisations and exercise frameworks
renderer_runtime_boundary: content build pipeline, visualisation library and exercise infrastructure are distinct but historically coupled
mobile_offline_accessibility: web courseware; mobile/accessibility quality requires activity-level review
ARA_usefulness: Important system precedent for coordinating narrative, visualisation and assessed action in one learning sequence
main_risks_or_limits: Strongly tied to CS/data structures and legacy Khan exercise infrastructure; not a generic extension contract

canonical_representation: Parsed molecular data models, query language, state tree, representations and scenes
learner_action_or_response: inspect, select, query, superpose and modify views of molecular structures
validation_and_assessment: scientific predicates and queries are available, but educational assessment must be supplied separately
feedback_model: visual/state feedback; educational explanations external
authoring_and_extension: modular plugin and state-transformation architecture with multiple data formats
renderer_runtime_boundary: data/model/query/state, geometry, renderer and UI are separated
mobile_offline_accessibility: WebGL-heavy; mobile and assistive use require targeted evaluation; large structures affect performance
ARA_usefulness: Strong domain precedent for chemistry/biology grammars and persisted semantic state rather than image snapshots
main_risks_or_limits: Very large scientific stack; 3D accessibility and offline data packages are difficult; not a learner-response model

canonical_representation: Map object with layers, geographic coordinates, markers, vectors and plugin-defined controls
learner_action_or_response: pan, zoom, select, add or manipulate geographic objects through application logic
validation_and_assessment: geospatial predicates and answer rules are external
feedback_model: continuous map feedback; pedagogical feedback external
authoring_and_extension: simple API and broad plugin ecosystem
renderer_runtime_boundary: geospatial model and browser renderer are closely integrated but application state is inspectable
mobile_offline_accessibility: mobile-first design; map accessibility and keyboard alternatives still require task-specific work; tile networks complicate offline use
ARA_usefulness: Useful engine candidate for geography, history, environment and spatial-data activities
main_risks_or_limits: Basemap licensing, network tile dependence, geographic precision and visual-only interaction can undermine portability/accessibility

canonical_representation: MusicXML parsed into a modifiable score model and rendered through VexFlow
learner_action_or_response: read, navigate and programmatically alter score presentation; not a full editor
validation_and_assessment: no educational scorer; note/rhythm/harmony validators would be separate
feedback_model: visual notation and optional highlighting; learning feedback external
authoring_and_extension: typed API, engraving rules and headless/browser rendering
renderer_runtime_boundary: MusicXML model, graphical score and renderer are distinct enough for an adapter
mobile_offline_accessibility: mobile rendering exists; recent Braille work is relevant; long scores are expensive; baseline playback is not core
ARA_usefulness: Shows that music requires a domain grammar such as MusicXML rather than generic formula or sequence resources
main_risks_or_limits: Renderer is not an editor or assessment engine; playback/media licensing and accessibility require separate capabilities

canonical_representation: Digital logic circuit graph with typed components, ports, wires and simulation state
learner_action_or_response: construct circuits and observe simulated behavior
validation_and_assessment: circuit topology and truth behavior can be checked deterministically; platform-specific educational grading needs inspection
feedback_model: simulation state and interactive book guidance
authoring_and_extension: web authoring platform plus interactive book
renderer_runtime_boundary: construction canvas, simulator and platform services are coupled
mobile_offline_accessibility: browser-based; dense drag interactions need keyboard/screen-reader alternatives and mobile review
ARA_usefulness: Strong domain precedent for learner-constructed circuits and stateful validation
main_risks_or_limits: Large application; circuit schema and simulator must not be copied without separating content, response and runtime contracts

canonical_representation: Text selections and annotation bodies aligned with the W3C Web Annotation model
learner_action_or_response: select ranges, create/update/delete annotations, tag or comment on passages
validation_and_assessment: annotation structure is validated by the library; educational claims and rubric assessment are external
feedback_model: selection/highlight feedback and application-defined annotation bodies
authoring_and_extension: JavaScript/React/TEI/PDF adapters with events and extensible payloads
renderer_runtime_boundary: annotation model, selectors and UI are separated
mobile_offline_accessibility: text-based and undoable; accessibility of selection and overlapping annotations requires explicit testing
ARA_usefulness: Strong candidate precedent for source analysis, argument annotation and evidence-linked responses in humanities/social sciences
main_risks_or_limits: Annotation correctness is task-dependent; offset/quote stability and collaborative conflicts need governance

canonical_representation: Language-specific rules and analysers exposed through Java, server and HTTP APIs
learner_action_or_response: submit multilingual text and receive detected spelling, grammar and style issues
validation_and_assessment: deterministic and statistical rules report matches and suggestions; not educational scoring
feedback_model: issue-local explanations/suggestions can support formative feedback
authoring_and_extension: large rule ecosystem and contribution process across languages
renderer_runtime_boundary: analysis engine can be run as service or embedded separately from editor
mobile_offline_accessibility: self-hosting possible but heavyweight; language coverage and false positives vary
ARA_usefulness: Useful validator precedent for language-production activities and locale-specific diagnostics
main_risks_or_limits: Proofreading quality is not equivalent to linguistic competence; LGPL integration and large resource footprint require review

canonical_representation: Chemistry simulation with domain objects, coefficients, visual molecule counts and game states
learner_action_or_response: manipulate coefficients and compare symbolic equations with particle/count representations
validation_and_assessment: simulation detects balanced states and task progress within its domain
feedback_model: immediate visual and game feedback
authoring_and_extension: PhET simulation code depends on a large shared framework stack
renderer_runtime_boundary: domain model, simulation state and Scenery-based UI exist across multiple repositories
mobile_offline_accessibility: single-file browser builds possible; accessibility and instrumentation depend on PhET framework; package stack is large
ARA_usefulness: Important precedent for coordinating symbolic and submicroscopic chemistry rather than treating reaction text as complete representation
main_risks_or_limits: Highly framework-specific and asset-heavy; simulation code is not a reusable general resource contract; license/trademark require careful review
